original_title: Acetylene as a C2 bridge for modular 1,4-dicarbonyl synthesis
title: Using both of acetylene's bonds instead of just one
blurb: Acetylene is dirt cheap but fine chemists mostly use it one bond at a time. This catalytic double hydroacylation threads a single acetylene molecule between two aldehydes or formamides via direct hydrogen-atom transfer, generating acyl and carbamoyl radicals with no decarbonylation and no sacrificial group. Couple two identical radicals and out come 1,4-diketones or 1,4-diamides in one operation.

original_title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
title: CeOx fixes cobalt carbide's slow step in turning CO2 into longer hydrocarbons
blurb: Cobalt carbide can push CO2 toward C2+ hydrocarbons via a CO2-Fischer-Tropsch route, but the CO hydrogenation step bottlenecks it. Dialing the Co/Ce ratio to 99 and letting dispersed CeOx interact with the Co2C gets a space-time yield of 106 mmol/g/h at 35% CO2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), beating every reported cobalt catalyst and matching some iron ones.

original_title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
title: Wiring sp-carbon into COFs to stop H2O2 electrosynthesis from stalling
blurb: Electrochemical H2O2 production via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction usually runs into sluggish charge transport and weak O2 activation, which is why the industry still leans on the energy-hungry anthraquinone process. Building sp-hybridized acetylene units into a covalent organic framework's vertices or linkers delocalizes charge through the lattice, going after both bottlenecks in one structural tweak.

original_title: π-Extended D–A Type [5]Helicenes: Cyano-Based Construction and Enhanced CPL Performance
title: A cyano twist that gets helicenes to actually glow
blurb: Two cyano D-A [5]helicenes made via Rosenmund-von Braun and Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons chemistry, where the cyano group strengthens intramolecular charge transfer and quiets the nonradiative decay enough to push fluorescence quantum yield to 39%. Swap substituents and the emission color shifts with it, and one variant, P[5]HE3CN, is the standout for circularly polarized luminescence.

original_title: Solvent Control of Cheletropic Recombination in Benzosultine-Derived ortho -Quinodimethane Diels–Alder Reactions
title: Why your o-QDM keeps turning back into SO2
blurb: Benzosultines are supposed to cough up o-quinodimethanes for Diels-Alder chemistry, but they love snapping back into benzosulfolenes via cheletropic SO2 recombination instead. Combined computation and experiment find the thermolysis runs through an o-QDM/SO2 encounter complex sitting right on the line between pericyclic and open-shell behavior, with TEMPO trapping confirming the C-S homolysis is reversible. Solvent choice is apparently the lever deciding which pathway wins.

original_title: Photoredox-catalyzed radical phosphinylation of [1.1.1]propellane via polarity match additions
title: Cracking open propellane's strained cage with a phosphinyl radical
blurb: Photoredox catalysis adds a phosphinyl radical across [1.1.1]propellane's strained core, with polarity matching keeping the radical addition selective.

original_title: Chemodivergent photoinitiated radical-polar crossover α- and α,β-C–H bond functionalisation of cyclic amine and ether scaffolds
title: One photocatalyst, two different C-H bonds, your choice
blurb: A photoinitiated radical-polar crossover on cyclic amines and ethers that can be steered to functionalize either the α C-H or the α,β C-H bond, same substrate class, different site depending on how you run it.

original_title: A practical demand-based model for determining cyclotron irradiation time in routine 18F-FDG production.
title: Right-sizing the cyclotron run for FDG orders
blurb: A demand-based model for picking cyclotron irradiation time for routine 18F-FDG production, matching beam time to how much FDG is actually needed instead of running a fixed protocol every batch. An ops fix, not a chemistry one.

original_title: Cu-Catalyzed Enantioconvergent Synthesis of N-Alkyl Amides from Racemic Alcohols
title: Turning racemic alcohols into one enantiomer of amide
blurb: A Cu-catalyzed radical relay takes racemic alcohols straight to enantioenriched N-alkyl amides, skipping the usual resolution step. The trick is β-scission of an oxidant-generated alkoxy radical erasing the alcohol's stereocenter before the enantioselective amidation rebuilds it, so both starting enantiomers funnel into the same product.

original_title: Solution and Mechanochemical Reactions of a Diphosphene with Elemental Sulfur
title: Grinding a diphosphene with sulfur gets you somewhere else entirely
blurb: Dissolve the bulky Eind-diphosphene with excess S8 in solution and the P=P bond cleaves down to a monomeric P(V) dithioxophosphorane, passing through a three-membered P2S ring intermediate on the way. Ball mill the same two reagents instead and the mechanochemical route heads somewhere different, same starting materials, different product depending on whether you bring a solvent.

original_title: 10 Start-Ups to Watch 2026: Nuclide Therapeutics builds leaner radiopharmaceuticals - Chemical & Engineering News
title: C&EN's radiopharma pick for 2026
blurb: Nuclide Therapeutics made C&EN's annual startups-to-watch list for building 'leaner' radiopharmaceuticals, whatever that ends up meaning in practice. Standard trade-press hype-list treatment, so judge them on the actual pipeline, not the blurb.

original_title: MPAThio Ligand-Accelerated Palladium-Catalyzed Nondirected Hydrogen Isotope Exchange of Arenes with D2O
title: Deuterating arenes faster by doubling up on ligands
blurb: A Pd catalyst paired with both a monoprotected aminoethyl thioether and an N-heteroarene ligand drives nondirected hydrogen isotope exchange with D2O to equilibrium in just 30 minutes at 105°C, or an hour at 90°C. Nondirected HIE on π-extended arenes is usually the slow, stubborn case, so the rate bump here is the actual news.

original_title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
title: Stiffer perovskite layers lase better
blurb: Comparing two 2D tin perovskites, the Ruddlesden-Popper BA2SnI4 built from a single-anchored butylammonium cation versus the Dion-Jacobson DABSnI4 built from a diammonium cation anchoring both sides. XRD and solid-state NMR show the ditopic cation locks the lattice down more rigidly, and that extra rigidity is what lets DABSnI4 hit amplified spontaneous emission. Tin perovskites still carry their usual stability baggage, but the structure-property link here is clean.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A cohort electron blood self-dose fraction and its propagated uncertainty for ¹²⁴I PET pre-therapy dosimetry in radioiodine therapy of differentiated thyroid cancer.
title: Tightening the error bars on I-124 PET thyroid dosimetry
blurb: A cohort-level self-dose fraction for blood, plus how its uncertainty propagates through pre-therapy I-124 PET dosimetry ahead of radioiodine treatment for differentiated thyroid cancer. Not a new method, just a sharper read on how much to trust the dose number you're planning the therapy around.

original_title: Navigating the Radical Oxo‐Functionalization of Alkenes Toward Ketones
title: Making ketones the radical way, mapped out
blurb: A review tracing the shift from classic two-electron carbonyl chemistry toward single-electron radical logic for building ketones directly from simple, commodity starting materials under mild conditions. Reads as a map of the field's current favorite tricks rather than a new reaction of its own.

original_title: Development And Validation of RP-HPLC Method for Simultaneous Estimation of Vitamin D3 And Vitamin K2 In Soft Gelatin Capsules
title: One HPLC run for both your vitamin D3 and K2
blurb: A validated reverse-phase HPLC method for quantifying vitamin D3 and K2 together in soft gelatin capsules. Squarely a QC-lab tool, not new chemistry.
venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Research and Applications

original_title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO 2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
title: Turns out you don't need the alkali metal, just fewer hydroxyl neighbors
blurb: Fe-catalyzed CO2-to-light-olefins usually leans on alkali or transition-metal promoters, but this one skips them by tuning the hydroxyl environment instead. A bit of guar gum breaks up the catalyst surface's hydrogen-bond network, leaving isolated terminal hydroxyls that open up active sites and help product desorb faster. One less metal to source, if it holds past lab scale.

original_title: Photocatalytic Divergent Skeletal Remodeling through Strain Release: Modular Access to Carbocycles and Heterocycles
title: Same strained bond, two different skeletons depending on the conditions
blurb: A photocatalytic strain-release reaction where one highly strained central bond gets reorganized two different ways: rigorously anhydrous conditions give 1,3-disubstituted naphthalenes, while a change in the reaction environment flips it over to pyrroles instead. Divergent access to carbocycles and heterocycles from the same starting skeleton is the whole pitch.

original_title: Cross-flow microfluidic photocatalysis with metal-organic framework thin films
title: Giving a MOF photocatalyst a crossflow instead of a beaker
blurb: A MOF thin-film photocatalyst paired with a cross-flow microfluidic reactor, so film thickness sets a known diffusion length, the film stays transparent enough for light to reach the active sites, and the crossflow handles the diffusion control batch reactors can't. Aimed at the usual MOF-photocatalysis complaint: fine surface chemistry undone by bad mass transport.

original_title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
title: Two manganese sites, one pressure gauge
blurb: A zero-dimensional manganese chloride packing both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn2+ centers into one lattice. Under pressure the octahedral site's red emission shifts linearly, and having both sites side by side in the same crystal is what lets the sensing calibrate itself instead of needing an external standard.

original_title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
title: An iron hydride that moves the amine before it adds it
blurb: MHAT hydroamination has mostly been stuck doing straightforward intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization. This iron-hydride catalyst instead runs a migratory version on allylamines, shuttling the amine over by one position through a finely tuned 1,2-migration before the new C-N bond locks in. A genuinely new mode of MHAT reactivity rather than another substrate-scope paper.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Recent Advances in Boryl Radical Chemistry: The Rise of Visible‐Light‐Mediated Lewis Base‐Coordinated Borane Chemistry
title: Boryl radicals, now mostly running on visible light
blurb: A review on how Lewis base-coordinated boranes, air-stable and easy to handle, became the standard boryl radical precursors, and how the field has shifted toward visible-light-driven hydroboration, borylation, and halogen/H/CN atom-transfer chemistry built on them. A survey of where radical organoboron synthesis stands now, not a new reaction.

original_title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
title: A cage that both grips its guest and locks it in
blurb: A D3-symmetric cage made from two curved hexabenzocoronene panels bridged by dibenzodiazocine units, forming three openings around a biconvex cavity shaped for aromatic guests. The point is combining two usually-separate host-guest modes, reversible thermodynamic binding and permanent kinetic trapping during cage formation, in one shape-complementary pocket.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Modular Access to Tetrasubstituted Allenes via 1,4-Dialkylation of 1,3-Enynes
title: Cobalt makes allenes from enynes, no ligand required
blurb: A cobalt-catalyzed 1,4-dialkylation of 1,3-enynes that stitches together fluoroalkyl halides and solid alkylzinc pivalates, no ligand needed and run under mild conditions. Tolerates aryl, alkyl, and silyl groups on the enyne and works across mono-, di-, per-fluoro, and bromo alkyl halides, so it's a genuinely broad route to tetrasubstituted fluoroalkylated allenes rather than one flashy example.

original_title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
title: Teaching ceria to swap out formyl hydrogens for deuterium
blurb: A Pt-on-ceria catalyst with extra surface oxygen vacancies runs hydrogen isotope exchange straight from D2O, no H2 gas needed, and gets over 95% deuterium incorporation specifically at the aldehyde's formyl position on p-methylbenzaldehyde. The site-selectivity is the actual trick, heterogeneous HIE catalysts usually can't pick a spot that cleanly.

original_title: De Novo Design of Enantioselective Artificial Metalloenzyme Photocatalysts Containing Metal Polypyridine Cofactors
title: Generative protein design builds an enzyme to pick one enantiomer of a metal catalyst
blurb: De novo protein scaffolds wrapped around metal polypyridine cofactors, designed computationally rather than found by screening, that make the resulting photocatalysis enantioselective. If it generalizes past the first examples, this is more about the design method working at all than this one catalyst.

original_title: Integrating Ion Mobility-Resolved Tandem Mass Spectrometry and Microcrystal Electron Diffraction for Structural Elucidation
title: Mass spec and electron diffraction team up to solve structures from almost nothing
blurb: Pairs ion-mobility tandem mass spec with microcrystal electron diffraction so full 3D structures come out of sub-microgram amounts of material, straight from reaction mixtures, no isolating pure compound first. Matters more for how little material a reaction screen now needs than for any single structure solved.

original_title: Fabrication of electrospun nanofibrous PVA/PEO/alginate sulfate water-stable mats via a gentle, non-toxic freeze-thawing cross-linking method as a potential drug delivery system.
title: Freeze-thawed nanofiber mats as a gentler drug delivery scaffold
blurb: Electrospun PVA/PEO/alginate sulfate mats cross-linked by freeze-thawing instead of a toxic chemical cross-linker, made water-stable and pitched as a drug delivery platform. Thin on specifics, so take it as proof of concept rather than a readout on how well it actually releases anything.

original_title: Directed evolution of laccase from Thermus thermophilus HB27 reveals a variant with enhanced high temperature catalytic activity and electrochemical properties
title: Screening 120,000 colonies to find a hotter laccase
blurb: Directed evolution of Thermus thermophilus laccase, screened by malachite green decolorization across a library of 1.2x10^5 colonies, turned up Q36H, a single mutation that boosts catalytic activity at high temperature over the wild-type. Bacterial laccases already beat fungal ones on stability, this just pushes one strain further.

original_title: Photochemical Radical Cascade Annulation of 6-Azauracils Enabled by CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals
title: Perovskite nanocrystals photocatalyze their way into 6-azauracils
blurb: 6-Azauracils are electron-poor and prone to falling apart, so direct annulation on them has been a hard sell. CsPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystals generate a nucleophilic aminomethyl radical from N-phenylglycine that adds across the ring's C=N bond and cascades into tetrahydroimidazole-fused products, using a photocatalyst that's neither the usual dye nor a transition-metal complex.

original_title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
title: A recyclable gold catalyst for turning alkynes into vinyl chlorides
blurb: Shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, normally a homogeneous reaction that's a pain to recover catalyst from, done instead with gold single atoms parked on activated carbon. Selective and reusable, and it skips the corrosive reagents shuttle catalysis usually needs.

original_title: Site-Specific N-Glycan-Resolved PK Assessment of Therapeutic Proteins Using Hybrid LBA-HRMS and LC-MS/MS
title: Pharmacokinetics broken down by which glycoform you're actually measuring
blurb: Aggregate PK numbers for therapeutic proteins average over glycoforms that clear the body at different rates, so this pairs LBA-HRMS and LC-MS/MS to track PK site-specifically by glycan. The point is that lot-to-lot comparisons based on the aggregate number could be hiding real differences underneath.

original_title: Synthesis of Diaryl α-Hydroxycarboxylic Acid Derivatives via Three-Component Reactions of o -Quinone Diimides with Alcohols and Diazo Compounds
title: A three-component route to diaryl alpha-hydroxy acids with a rhodium assist
blurb: Rhodium-catalyzed three-component coupling of o-quinone diimides, alcohols, and diazo compounds, going through an oxonium ylide intermediate trapped by the arylating agent, builds diaryl alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acids with an oxa-quaternary center. Broad substrate scope, scaled up, and run on a late-stage complex molecule, so it's pitched as more than a model-substrate curiosity.

original_title: Applications of Single-Atom Alloys in Thermal, Electro, and Photo Catalysis
title: Single-atom alloys, the 2020 review's sequel
blurb: A follow-up to their 2020 Chem Rev on single-atom alloys, catalysts that pin isolated reactive metal atoms into a host metal surface so each one acts as its own well-defined site. The payoff is selectivity and resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering that bulk alloys don't get, plus some systems that dodge the usual scaling relationships limiting conventional catalysts. It's a review, so don't expect new chemistry, just the state of the field since last time.

original_title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
title: A cerium MOF that flips its own fluorescence switch
blurb: An Eu-doped Ce-MOF/CTF interface where oxidation flips Ce3+ to Ce4+ and rewires the charge-transfer network, giving a dual-mode fluorescence readout for H2O2. Nice mechanism if you like valence states doing the sensing work instead of a separate reporter dye.

original_title: Multivalent Avidity in C-type Lectins: How Glycan Surface Density and Presentation Define Superselective Recognition by DC-SIGN
title: DC-SIGN doesn't care about weak binders until there's enough of them
blurb: Using a tetravalent DC-SIGN construct, they work out how glycan density and spacing on a surface combine with the lectin's four weak, promiscuous binding sites to produce sharp, superselective recognition. Selectivity here isn't any one CRD being picky, it's what happens once enough of them engage at once.

original_title: Beyond the solvent fog: watching molecules dance in the crowd
title: Watching a reaction happen through the solvent instead of around it
blurb: Time-resolved X-ray liquidography gets used to track a classic reaction step by step in solution, the part usually hidden behind solvent noise. A methods piece more than a new reaction, but seeing the intermediates directly instead of inferring them is the actual news.

original_title: A Pathology-Responsive Hydrogel with On-Demand Ion Release for Microenvironment Remodeling and Diabetic Wound Regeneration.
title: A wound dressing that releases ions when it senses trouble
blurb: A hydrogel for diabetic wounds that reads the pathological microenvironment and releases ions on demand to remodel it and push regeneration along. Light on detail beyond that, but triggering release off the wound's own state rather than a fixed dose is the idea worth tracking.

original_title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
title: Borrowing photosynthesis's wiring to quiet down a fluorescent probe
blurb: Fluorescent probes for single-cell diagnosis are usually held back by leaky background signal from incomplete control over electron transfer inside the probe itself. They borrow the spatial organization photosynthetic pigments use for coherent energy transport and build it into probe assemblies to steer electron transfer between molecules instead, cutting that background. Quantum chemistry doing probe design is the hook, not just another dye.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: BMS Planning Regulatory Filing for RayzeBio’s GEP-NET Radiopharmaceutical - GenomeWeb
title: RayzeBio's GEP-NET radiopharmaceutical heads toward the FDA
blurb: BMS is lining up a regulatory filing for the GEP-NET radiopharmaceutical it picked up in the RayzeBio acquisition. Filing news, not trial data, but it's the clearest sign yet that program is actually moving toward approval.

original_title: A Composition-Matched Intermediate Reveals Site-Specific Symmetry Evolution with Retained Second-Harmonic Generation in Supertetrahedral Sulfides
title: A middle sibling that pins down which substitution does what
blurb: In the supertetrahedral sulfide series Rb10Zn4Sn4S17 to Cs10Cd4Sn4S17, they made Cs10Zn4Sn4S17 as a composition-matched midpoint, not a reaction intermediate, which separates what the A-site Rb/Cs swap does from what the M-site Zn/Cd swap does. Symmetry shifts site by site, but the second-harmonic generation survives the whole way, which is the part that actually matters for using these as NLO materials.

original_title: A Statistical Mechanics Perspective on Memory and Forgetting in Nonequilibrated Polymer Films
title: Polymer films remember their past, and someone's trying to model the forgetting
blurb: Spin-coated polymer films carry stresses from how they were made, and relaxing those away is really the system erasing that memory, not just ordinary viscoelastic decay. Conventional equilibrium polymer dynamics only explains part of it, so this pushes toward a statistical-mechanics framework for the forgetting itself. A perspective piece, so judge it on whether the framework predicts anything later.

original_title: Cation-Gated Interfacial Electrocatalysis: Mechanisms and Effects of Alkali and Alkaline Earth Metal Cations
title: The electrolyte's cations were never just along for the ride
blurb: A review arguing alkali and alkaline earth cations, Li+ through Ba2+, actively shape electrocatalysis rather than just balancing charge, across hydrogen evolution/oxidation, oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, CO2 reduction, and nitrate reduction. The effects run through the double layer, interfacial fields, local pH, and water networks, and they're reaction-specific, so there's no single story, just five of them stapled together.

original_title: AKIR001 radiopharmaceutical shows no dose-limiting toxicities in eight patients - The Clinical Trial Vanguard
title: Another radiopharmaceutical clears the bar of not hurting anyone
blurb: AKIR001 ran through eight patients with no dose-limiting toxicities, which is phase 1 safety data and nothing more. Eight patients is a rounding error and there's no efficacy signal here, just a green light to keep dosing.

original_title: Simulating Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
title: A workaround for VQE's overhead in quantum molecular dynamics
blurb: Ab initio molecular dynamics and vibrational analysis on quantum computers have mostly run through VQE, whose deep circuits and heavy measurement overhead make it a slog. This extends sample-based quantum diagonalization, a non-variational sampling approach, to both tasks and actually runs it on noisy hardware rather than idealized simulation. The pitch is pairing classical sampling with the quantum device instead of leaning on the device for everything.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Magnetically Induced Functional Fe 3 O 4 /Iron Foam Catalysts for Enhanced CO 2 ‐Assisted Ethane Dehydrogenation
title: Magnetic heating shaves 200°C off CO2-assisted ethane dehydrogenation
blurb: Fe3O4 stuck onto iron foam, heated by an alternating magnetic field instead of a furnace, hits comparable ethane-to-ethylene conversion at 500°C that conventional thermal catalysis needs 200°C more to match. It also doubles as CO2 conversion, so the olefin and the greenhouse gas get handled in the same pot. Whether the induction catalyst holds up outside this setup is the part worth watching.

original_title: Peptide-AuNP-drug conjugate-integrated photocrosslinkable hydrogel with pH/glutathione dual-responsive drug delivery and NIR-triggered heating for combined chemo-photothermal treatment.
title: A hydrogel that releases its drug and then cooks the tumor
blurb: Peptide-gold nanoparticle-drug conjugates built into a photocrosslinkable hydrogel that dumps its payload when pH or glutathione shifts, with NIR light adding a thermal kick on top for combined chemo-photothermal treatment. Clever stacking of triggers, but it's the usual hydrogel-in-a-dish demo until someone runs it in an animal.

original_title: Fabrication and characterization of cross-linked polymer hydrogel encapsulated with Nisin for wound dressing applications.
title: Nisin gets locked into a hydrogel for wound dressings
blurb: A crosslinked polymer hydrogel loaded with the bacteriocin nisin, pitched for wound dressing use. What's here is fabrication and characterization, so the actual antimicrobial performance numbers are the thing to chase down before getting excited.

original_title: Avenzo Therapeutics Announces Oral Presentation of Phase 1 Data for VBC103 (AVZO-103), a Potentially Differentiated Nectin-4/TROP2 Bispecific Antibody-Drug Conjugate, by Partner VelaVigo at ESMO Asia Congress 2026 - FinancialContent
title: Avenzo's bispecific ADC gets its Phase 1 data an airing at ESMO Asia
blurb: VBC103 (AVZO-103), a Nectin-4/TROP2 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate, gets its Phase 1 data presented orally by partner VelaVigo at ESMO Asia 2026. This is the presentation announcement, not the data itself, so the actual numbers are still to come.

original_title: Green radiochemistry and sustainability in radiopharmaceutical sciences
title: Someone's asking if radiopharmaceuticals can be made less wasteful
blurb: A review on green radiochemistry and sustainability in radiopharmaceutical sciences. More framing than new data, but a field built on short-lived isotopes and one-shot syntheses probably deserves the scrutiny.

original_title: Perturbation of the Electron Transport Chain by Guanidinium‐Based Cationic Polymers Induces Metabolic Collapse in Persister‐Enriched Bacterial Populations
title: Guanidinium polymers hit bacterial persisters where they're not sleeping
blurb: Persisters are supposed to be dormant, but this guanidinium-based cationic polymer (PO3G) preferentially kills them by wrecking electron transport chain activity, triggering sustained superoxide damage afterward. Makes the case that persister 'quiescence' is actually a specific vulnerability, at least against this one polymer class.

original_title: Applicability of the defined solid angle method to the activity measurement of α-emitters for targeted radionuclide therapy.
title: Weighing alpha emitters by the solid angle they cover
blurb: Tests whether the defined solid angle method, a standard way of pinning down source activity, actually holds up for alpha-emitters used in targeted radionuclide therapy. Not glamorous, but dosing these therapies correctly depends on getting the activity measurement right in the first place.

original_title: A (177)Lu-labeled Inetetamab theranostic conjugate with dual cytotoxic and stromal-depleting activities for targeted radionuclide therapy of HER2-positive breast cancer.
title: Lu-177 hitches a ride on an anti-HER2 antibody with a side job clearing stroma
blurb: Inetetamab, an anti-HER2 antibody, gets conjugated to Lu-177 for a theranostic billed as doing two things at once: killing HER2-positive breast cancer cells directly and depleting the stroma around them. The stromal-depleting angle is the interesting part, since most radioconjugate work only goes after the tumor cells themselves.

original_title: Applicability of the defined solid angle method to the activity measurement of α-emitters for targeted radionuclide therapy
title: How much activity is actually in your alpha-emitter source
blurb: Otsuka and colleagues test the defined solid angle method for measuring alpha-emitter activity for targeted radionuclide therapy, set to run in Applied Radiation and Isotopes' January 2027 issue. Dry metrology work, but if the activity assay is off, the dose downstream is off too.

original_title: Stereoselective Defluorinative Thiolation of gem -Difluoroalkenes with Thiols via Nucleophilic Substitution
title: Swapping fluorine for sulfur without a metal in sight
blurb: A transition-metal-free, base-promoted defluorinative thiolation turns gem-difluoroalkenes into monofluoroalkenyl sulfides through plain nucleophilic substitution, with good yields and Z/E selectivity up to 24:1. Monofluoroalkenes already get used as enol and amide mimics in drug discovery, and this reaches them without the usual metal-catalyst baggage.

original_title: One‐Pot Construction of Amine‐Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks via Photoredox‐Catalyzed Reductive Amination
title: Amine-linked COFs finally get a photoredox route
blurb: The first photocatalytic synthesis of amine-linked covalent organic frameworks, built in one pot via photoredox-catalyzed reductive amination under ambient conditions. Amine linkages pack in more basic sites and hold up better than the usual imine-linked versions, and until now nobody had a light-driven way to make them.

original_title: A High-Throughput Chemical Proteomic Approach for Profiling Serum CA19-9 Protein Carriers and Their Characterization in Patients with Elevated CA19-9 Levels
title: Finding out which proteins are actually carrying CA19-9
blurb: CA19-9 is the pancreatic cancer marker everyone uses and everyone knows throws false positives from plain inflammation. This group built a 96-well chemical proteomics platform with a trifunctional probe that photo-crosslinks anti-CA19-9 antibodies to their protein carriers straight from microliters of serum, fast enough to actually profile patients instead of grinding through one sample at a time. If carrier identity tracks with malignancy versus inflammation, that's the specificity fix CA19-9 has needed for decades.

original_title: Antibody–drug conjugates in lung cancer: clinical development, therapeutic advances, and emerging challenges
title: The ADC landscape for lung cancer, mapped
blurb: A review tracking where antibody-drug conjugates stand across NSCLC and small cell lung cancer, payloads, targets, mechanisms, and which ones are actually moving through the clinic. Useful as a map, not a result.

original_title: Broadly Accessible and Highly Active Hydrophosphination Catalysis With Simple Calcium Compounds in DMSO Solution
title: Calcium quietly becomes a hydrophosphination catalyst that works on everything
blurb: Simple, cheap calcium precatalysts running hydrophosphination across more than 120 substrates, styrenes, Michael acceptors, dienes, heterocumulenes, alkynes, even unactivated and natural alkenes, most clearing 90% conversion. Broadest scope reported for this reaction, and it gets there with an abundant metal instead of the usual precious-metal suspects.

original_title: Practical C(sp3)–F Bond Construction via Metal-Free Heterogeneous Photodecarboxylative Fluorination in Continuous Flow
title: Turning carboxylic acids into C–F bonds with light instead of metal
blurb: A metal-free photocatalytic decarboxylative fluorination using g-C3N4 under visible light, with good generality on activated aliphatic acids and late-stage pharma scaffolds, and the catalyst survives seven recycling runs. They back it up with a gram-scale continuous-flow run, so this isn't just a vial-scale curiosity.

original_title: Integrated High-Throughput Mass Spectrometry Framework for Multiplexed Substrate Screening in Enzyme Discovery and Development
title: A mass spec setup built to screen enzymes against many substrates at once
blurb: An integrated high-throughput MS framework doing both targeted quantitation and untargeted product discovery on biocatalytic reactions, aimed at the kind of multiplexed substrate screening regular single-quadrupole LC-MS can't keep up with. More plumbing than discovery, but the kind of tool that quietly speeds up enzyme hunting.

original_title: From Chlorogermanes to Carbon–Germanium Bonds: Electrochemical Strategies for Modular Germylation
title: Making carbon-germanium bonds without the usual stoichiometric reductants
blurb: A conspectus on electrochemical routes from chlorogermanes to C-Ge bonds, going after a gap silicon and tin chemistry closed long ago but germanium hasn't, since current methods still mostly lean on preformed organometallics or hydrogermanes. Organogermanium's getting attention as a bioisostere, so a general, modular method matters more than it sounds.

original_title: Albumin-Binding Moieties Tune the Pharmacokinetics and Tumor Uptake of (177)Lu-Labeled GRPR Radioligands.
title: Giving Lu-177 GRPR radioligands an albumin handle to stick around longer
blurb: Albumin-binding moieties attached to Lu-177-labeled GRPR radioligands to tune pharmacokinetics and tumor uptake, the standard trick for keeping a radiotherapeutic in circulation longer before it clears.

original_title: Pd(II)-Catalyzed Decarboxylative ortho -Amidation of Benzyl Thiocyanates with Oxamic Acids Unveiling -SCN as a Bidentate Directing Group
title: Thiocyanate gets promoted to directing group
blurb: Pd(II)-catalyzed ortho-amidation of benzyl thiocyanates with oxamic acids, using AgOAc as the oxidant, with -SCN doing double duty as a weak but multicoordinating directing group instead of just sitting there as a substituent. Regiospecific and broad across substituted, secondary, and heterocyclic thiocyanates.

original_title: Water-Mediated Electrochemical Sulfonylation of Alkynes: Switchable Access to Alkynyl versus Alkenyl Sulfones
title: Dialing between alkynyl and alkenyl sulfones just by tuning current and water
blurb: An electrochemical sulfonylation of alkynes with thiophenols where water supplies both the hydrogen and the oxygen, and tweaking current intensity and water dosage flips the product between alkynyl and alkenyl sulfones. No metal catalyst, no hazardous oxidant, and broad substrate scope claimed too.

original_title: Polyoxometalate‐Scaffolded Perylene Diimide Dimers: Preorganization and Dynamic Charge Regulation for Enhanced and Durable Photosensitization
title: A polyoxometalate scaffold that locks perylene diimides into a durable photosensitizer
blurb: Rigid, redox-active POM clusters pin two perylene diimides into a tight, parallel-displaced stack, forcing fast excimer formation while also tuning the charge dynamics that come with it. Pulling off structural preorganization and dynamic charge regulation at once is the hard part, and it's what gets them the enhanced, more durable photosensitization.

original_title: Intramolecular Stereospecific Skeletal Rearrangement via Nonclassical Carbocations
title: Nonclassical carbocations rebuild a whole skeleton without scrambling stereochemistry
blurb: A Lewis acid pushes fully substituted stereocenters through nonclassical cyclopropylcarbinyl cation intermediates, and the carbon skeleton rearranges completely while regio- and diastereoselectivity stay excellent. Mostly a demonstration that these textbook-unstable intermediates can be steered on purpose instead of just invoked after the fact to explain a mechanism.

original_title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
title: One Rh/photoredox system, two different chiral sulfoximine scaffolds
blurb: A visible-light Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid system takes the same sulfoximine and alkyne feedstocks and, just by tuning conditions, steers C–H activation toward two distinct chiral-at-sulfur products. Asymmetric versions of photoredox/metal-catalyzed C–H activation are still thin on the ground, so the divergent selectivity is the actual point, not the enantioselectivity by itself.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Radioligand Plus Radiation Delays Prostate Cancer Progression to 17.6 Months - Cure Today
title: Radiation plus radioligand therapy buys prostate cancer patients more time
blurb: Adding radiation to radioligand therapy pushed progression-free survival to 17.6 months. That's the whole headline number on offer here, no comparator or trial design to weigh it against yet.

original_title: Photocatalyzed Trifluoromethylamidative Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Access to Trifluoromethylamidyl Cyclobutenes
title: Cracking open bicyclobutanes to install N-CF3 groups
blurb: A photocatalytic NCF3 radical-transfer reaction tears open donor-acceptor bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes and delivers trifluoromethylamidyl cyclobutenes that were apparently not accessible before. N-CF3 chemistry has mostly been stuck doing simple substitutions, so running the radical through an sp3 carbon via ring strain is the real move.

original_title: Calix[n]BODIPYs: One-Pot Assembly of Strain-Relieved Methylene-Bridged Macrocycles with Bright Fluorescence
title: BODIPYs stitched into a macrocycle by their own Friedel-Crafts carbocation
blurb: BF3 generates a benzylic carbocation right on a hydroxymethyl-BODIPY precursor, which then alkylates its way onto neighboring BODIPY units, one pot, closing a calix-like macrocycle. The payoff shows up in the numbers: molar extinction coefficients up to 7.39×10^5 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ and fluorescence quantum yields up to 0.92, bright even by BODIPY standards.

original_title: Bicyclic BODIPY-Submonoazaporphyrin Hybrids via a Catalyst-Free SNAr Strategy: Coexisting Local Aromaticity and Global Antiaromaticity with Broad NIR-II Absorption
title: A porphyrinoid that's locally aromatic and globally antiaromatic at once
blurb: Catalyst-free SNAr bolts BODIPY onto submonoazaporphyrin, and the resulting hybrid is simultaneously 14π aromatic in its local rings and 28π antiaromatic overall, confirmed by NMR and calculations rather than just claimed. It also absorbs cleanly from 300 to 1400 nm into the NIR-II window, so there's a real materials payoff attached to the aromaticity bookkeeping.

original_title: Copper(II) Acetate-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of N -(2-Arylacetyl)-1,3-oxazolidin-2-ones to 1,2-Dicarbonyl Compounds
title: Room-temperature copper and air turn arylacetyl oxazolidinones into diketones
blurb: Cu(OAc)2 with phenanthroline, in DMSO, at just 30°C, oxidizes arylacetyl oxazolidinones to 1,2-dicarbonyls with no base, no extra oxidant, and no multi-hour reflux. The resulting α-keto imides are one step from α-keto esters, amides, or α-hydroxy acids, so this reads as a cleaner on-ramp to a useful building block rather than a new reaction for its own sake.

original_title: Identification of Readily Accessible Manganese Catalysts Enables Multi-gram Scale Enantioselective γ-C(sp 3 )‒H Lactonization of Carboxylic Acids
title: Cheap manganese catalysts scale up C-H lactonization from milligrams to grams
blurb: Carboxylic-acid-directed γ-C(sp3)-H lactonization is a neat way to build lactones straight from the acid, but it's usually gated by harsh conditions and pricey catalysts. Swapping in readily accessible manganese catalysts gets the enantioselective version running at multi-gram scale, which is the part that matters if anyone outside a methods paper wants to actually use it.

original_title: Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Tricrilactones D and F, Crispatumine I, and 2,3- trans -Crispatumine I
title: One cascade, four natural products, by following the proposed biosynthesis
blurb: A one-pot three-component cascade built around protrilactione A, the purported biosynthetic precursor, assembles the shared 9/5/6 spirocyclic lactone core directly. Swapping the aldehyde and β-ketolactone inputs reaches tricrilactones D and F plus both crispatumine I diastereomers, each in 13 steps, which doubles as a decent argument that the proposed biosynthesis is actually right.

original_title: Deacylative Functionalization of Ketones via Radical-Triggered Alkyl–Acyl Bond Cleavage
title: Methyl ketones give up their acyl group by cheating toward aromaticity
blurb: No metal and no UV lamp required: methyl ketones get coaxed into pre-aromatic intermediates where the drive to aromatize snaps the α-C–C bond and leaves a carbon-centered radical behind. That radical then gets funneled into alkenylation, alkynylation, heteroarylation, or oxime etherification, so one simple deacylation step covers a surprisingly wide spread of products.

original_title: Photocatalytic Scaffold Hopping of Cyclobutanols to Cyclopentanols via Single-Carbon Insertion into C–C σ-Bonds
title: Cyclobutanols become cyclopentanols by inserting one carbon
blurb: Photocatalytic skeletal editing that inserts a single carbon into a cyclobutanol's strained C-C sigma bond, hopping straight to the cyclopentanol instead of going through the usual semipinacol rearrangement. Mild conditions, good yields, another tool for the single-atom-insertion pile.

original_title: Sequential Hydrogen Atom Transfer‐Mediated Electrochemical Diselenylation of Oxindoles to Access Antifungal gem ‐Diselenides
title: Electrochemistry, not a metal, bolts diselenides onto oxindoles
blurb: Direct C(sp3)-H gem-diselenylation of oxindoles run electrochemically with no oxidant and no metal, iodide mediating what looks like a radical pathway. Broad substrate scope, gram-scale, works on late-stage drug molecules, and the products come out antifungal.

original_title: Transformation of Aromatic Feedstocks into Value-Added Products via Biocatalytic Primary Amination
title: Engineered hemoproteins put an amine straight onto an arene
blurb: Evolved protoglobin variants do enantioselective aminative dearomatization and regioselective aryl C(sp2)-H amination on aromatic feedstocks, in water, using cheap hydroxylamine as the nitrogen source. Started from a variant with barely any activity and got there by directed evolution, which is usually the more interesting part of these stories than the first hit.

original_title: Manganese-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of α-Substituted Tetralones via Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
title: Manganese doing the asymmetric hydrogenation precious metals usually do
blurb: Dynamic kinetic resolution hydrogenation of alpha-substituted tetralones with manganese standing in for the usual Ir or Ru, hitting up to 99% yield, 99% ee, and >20:1 dr, with two stereocenters set at once. Holds up at gram scale too.

original_title: Recent Advances in Triplet Free‐Carbene Transfer Chemistry
title: Trying to make carbenes behave like diradicals on command
blurb: A review on photoinduced free-carbene transfer chemistry, where the hard part is steering generation toward the triplet, diradical-character carbene instead of the default singlet. Survey-level, so no single result here, just where the selectivity problem stands.

original_title: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
title: Peroxygenases moonlighting as enantioselective alcohol oxidation catalysts
blurb: Unspecific peroxygenases, usually an afterthought next to alcohol dehydrogenases and copper/flavin oxidases, get run through three different enantioselective alcohol oxidation setups, including kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols and desymmetrization of meso-diols. Mostly notable because nobody had bothered checking if UPOs could do this at all.

original_title: Recent Advances in Functional Group Transpositions in Arenes and Heteroarenes
title: Actually relocating a substituent on an arene, not just rearranging around it
blurb: A review drawing the line between classical aromatic rearrangements like Smiles, Claisen, and Bamberger, which always leave a residual group behind at the original ipso carbon, and the rarer reactions that net-relocate a substituent with nothing left behind. The real transpositions, framed as underdeveloped next to their more famous cousins.

original_title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
title: Getting around the aqueous aluminum battery's additive catch-22
blurb: Additives that loosen Al3+'s brutal solvation shell usually wreck reversibility anyway, either collapsing the dielectric or locking the kinetics. This electrolyte pairs Al(OTf)3 with DMSO and FEC asymmetrically to loosen the coordination without that tradeoff. If it generalizes, that additive paradox has been the real blocker for these batteries.

original_title: Alkyl-BODIPYs as a Self-Photoredox Catalyst for their Oxidative Hydroxymethylation
title: BODIPYs catalyzing their own oxidation, no separate photocatalyst needed
blurb: Alkylated BODIPYs absorb the light and drive their own oxidation to the hydroxymethyl derivative in one pot, with an NHC-H quencher handling the electron transfer. Stern-Volmer data backs a reductive-quenching mechanism. Catalyst-free only in the sense that the substrate is doing the catalyzing.

original_title: Dihydrogen Phosphate Anion-Templated Synthesis of Urethane-Based Macrocycle Containing Perfluoroalkyl Chain
title: A phosphate anion templates a perfluoroalkyl macrocycle
blurb: H2PO4- preorganizes the cyclization transition state through hydrogen bonding, DFT in hand to back it up, and bumps up the yield of a urethane macrocycle carrying a long perfluoroalkyl chain. The fluoroalkyl chain also quietly acidifies the neighboring CH2, the kind of side effect these template papers tend to bury.

original_title: Artificial Light-Harvesting Nanotubes: Intermolecular Charge Transfer beyond the Exciton Model
title: Solving the nanotube light-harvesting puzzle without ditching the exciton model
blurb: Cryo-EM says these self-assembled C8S3 dye nanotubes pack brick-layer, not the herringbone arrangement everyone assumed to explain the old absorption and dichroism data. The exciton model survives anyway, once you let it account for intermolecular charge transfer alongside the usual exciton coupling.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Unlocking the Tertiary Nitrogen Effect in 3D Anisotropic Covalent Organic Frameworks to Achieve Record Iodine Capture under Industrial Conditions
title: COFs built for the one job iodine scrubbers keep failing at
blurb: Two new 3D COFs (ECUT-COF-99 and ECUT-COF-100) built off a minimal-transitivity flu-derived net, with tertiary nitrogens doing the capturing. ECUT-COF-100 posts an ultrahigh iodine uptake under actual industrial conditions, where most adsorbents just don't.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Triple Atom Transfer-Enabled α-C(sp3)-H Aminomethylation of Aliphatic Amines: General and Modular Access to Vicinal Diamines
title: Three atom transfers deep to get vicinal diamines from amines
blurb: A photocatalytic route chains halogen-atom transfer into an intramolecular 1,5-HAT to aminomethylate the α-C-H of aliphatic amines directly, turning cheap feedstock amines into vicinal diamines, including the tertiary-alkylamine kind that's otherwise annoying to build.

original_title: Highly Diastereoselective Synthesis of Trifluoromethylated Spirocyclopropanes from 2-(2′-Ketoalkyl)-1,3-Indandiones and CF3-Imidoyl Sulfoxonium Ylides
title: Trifluoromethylated spirocyclopropanes, no metal required
blurb: Sulfoxonium ylides carrying the CF3-imidoyl group react with indandione-derived ketones in a base-mediated cascade to build spirocyclopropanes, metal-free, with good to excellent yields and diastereoselectivity holding across a broad substrate scope. Runs on gram scale too.

original_title: Peroullazines: Synthesis, Structure, and Optoelectronic Properties
title: Swap a pyrene ring for pyrrole and see what you get
blurb: Ullazine is pyrene's five-membered-ring cousin, a heteroaromatic swap that shifts the electronics. This paper pushes it further with peroullazines, extended derivatives whose synthesis, structure, and optoelectronic properties they work out as a materials-chemistry play.

original_title: Controlled Generation of Unstabilized N -Alkyl Nitrile Imines Enables Regioselective (3 + 2) Cycloadditions with Diverse Dipolarophiles
title: N-alkyl nitrile imines finally get tamed into 3+2 chemistry
blurb: These intermediates have been too unstable to use for intermolecular cycloadditions until now. Generated in situ, they cycloadd regioselectively with both activated and unactivated alkenes and alkynes to give N-alkyl pyrazolines and pyrazoles, and the method scales: a key pyrazole fragment for lenacapavir comes out in 79% over two steps on gram scale.

original_title: An experimentally-validated principle for selectivity in endergonic reactions
title: Thermodynamic and kinetic control don't cover endergonic reactions, so here's a third rule
blurb: For reactions running uphill, with species forming and breaking down at once, neither product free energy nor transition-state energy sets the selectivity. What does, per this paper, is the degree of turnover-frequency control each intermediate exerts along the kinetic barrier, backed by experiment rather than just theory.

original_title: ARID1B promotes DNA end resection via MDC1 and co-transactivation of DNA repair genes with c-MYC in small cell lung cancer
title: ARID1B teams up with c-MYC to keep small cell lung cancer repairing its own DNA
blurb: ARID1B is overexpressed in SCLC versus normal lung or adenocarcinoma, and knocking it down cripples proliferation and tumor growth both in vitro and in vivo. The mechanism is that it promotes DNA end resection via MDC1 and co-transactivates repair genes alongside c-MYC, which reads like a resistance pathway worth targeting, not just another overexpression finding.

original_title: A Highly Stable Cyclic (Amino)(Aryl)Nitrenium Radical Dication Exhibiting Temperature-Dependent Radical Bistability Maruti Suryavansi,a Manas Khatua,b,d Bappaditya Goswami,c Apurba Kumar Pal,a Subhas Samanta,*d and K. Geetharani*
title: A nitrenium radical that doesn't fall apart the moment you look at it
blurb: NHC-stabilized, isolated in the solid state and confirmed by X-ray, this cyclic amino(aryl)nitrenium radical dication shrugs off air, water, strong acid and base, and high temperature, which transient organic radicals are not supposed to do. It also flips between bistable radical states with temperature, the first time this class has been caged this well.

original_title: Nonconventional Liquid Crystals with a Helicene-Containing Core: Synthesis, Columnar Mesomorphism, Photoluminescence, and Electron Conductivity
title: Helicene cores that happen to also be liquid crystals
blurb: Two rounds of BuLi-assisted SNAr stitch a difluorinated [5]helicene core onto four alkoxy chains, giving Janus-like mesogens. The payoff is an unusually rich columnar mesophase range, hexagonal through rectangular to lamellar, plus photoluminescence and electron conductivity along for the ride.

original_title: Synthesis and Photophysical Properties of Thiazole/Benzothiazole‐Fused Nonastarazines: Extending the Core and Tuning Emission via Positional Substitution
title: Swapping pyridine for thiazole on nonastarazine arms
blurb: Boron-locked three-armed nonastarazines fused with thiazole or benzothiazole instead of the previous pyridine rings. Crystal structures stay nearly planar, with the boron-bound phenyls twisting out of the plane to keep the dyes from stacking and crashing out of solution. The ring swap does real electronic work, tuning emission just by where the substituents sit.

original_title: Self-assembly of a giant heterometallic polyoxovanadate with catalytic activity for epoxidation of alkenes
title: 128 vanadium ions walk into a flask
blurb: Self-assembly in water, with tartaric acid directing the structure, yields the largest polyoxovanadate cluster on record: a manganese-bridged tetramer built from 128 V ions. It's also an active epoxidation catalyst for alkenes, not just a crystallography trophy, though getting POVs this size to self-assemble at all has apparently been the hard part.

original_title: Efficient Long-Wavelength Through-Space Charge Transfer Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence in Conformationally Adaptive Emitters without Conformational Locking
title: Red TADF emission without locking the molecule down
blurb: Long-wavelength through-space charge-transfer TADF usually means bolting the donor and acceptor into a rigid frame. This S-shaped phenoxazine/xanthene/dibenzophenazine emitter stays conformationally loose by NMR and computation, and still gets efficient orange-to-red TADF out of it.

original_title: Direct Synthesis of α‐Amino Ketones From Aldehydes and Amines via Photocatalytic In Situ Imines Hydroacylation
title: Skip making the imine, just photocatalyze straight to amino ketones
blurb: Hydroacylation usually needs the imine made and isolated first. This one-pot photocatalytic route, TBADT plus a touch of HBr, forms the imine in situ from aldehyde and amine and hydroacylates it on the spot, landing directly on α-amino ketones.
